Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

IChop 0.1.2.9000

This is the first entry in the changelog. It describes the package as it stands; later entries will list changes relative to this version.

  • The package is renamed from GICHighDimension to IChop (information criterion selection by Hopfield networks). The Julia version is renamed from GICVariableSelection to IChop.jl.

Variable selection

  • GICSelection() selects variables by a Hopfield-network coordinate search: it visits the candidate variables in random order, proposes adding or removing each one, and keeps the move when the information criterion improves (Xiao and Walker, 2026, Statistics and Computing, doi:10.1007/s11222-026-10853-5).
  • GICSelectionBoltzmann() runs the same search but also accepts a move that lowers the criterion, with probability 1/(1 + e^{\Delta/T}), so it can leave a local optimum.
  • Both return the criterion value and the selected variables after each step; GICSelection() also returns elapsed, the time since the search started.
  • k caps the model size, and models never exceed n - 1 variables, so the search also works when p > n.
  • Vector responses and matrix responses (several outcomes sharing the same predictors) are supported.

Information criteria

  • AIC, AICc, BIC, CAIC, CAICF, SIC, GIC2–GIC6, EBIC and AttIC, each as a Calculate_*() function that scores a single model. See ?information_criteria for their penalties and references.
  • EBIC’s \gamma is set with the gamma argument (default 0.6).

Speed

  • The search never forms the n \times n hat matrix. Every criterion is computed from X^\top Y and (X^\top X)^{-1}, and each move is scored with a rank-one update at O(nK + K^2) cost for a model with K variables. On simulated data this is 38–371 times faster than version 0.1.2.
  • The search runs in Julia, and the Julia code is loaded once per session. setup_julia() connects R to Julia and install_julia_packages() installs the Julia packages the package needs.
  • GICSelection() and GICSelectionBoltzmann() pass the criterion to Julia by name. Passing the function itself turned it into an R wrapper that the search did not recognise, so calls from R fell back to refitting every candidate model; they are now 17–25 times faster (n = 1000, p = 500).

Generalized linear models

  • LP_to_Y() simulates responses from a linear predictor, Y_to_LP() maps responses to the linear-predictor scale before selection, and Beta_estimate() fits the selected model. They support Normal, Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Gamma, Exponential, InverseGaussian, NegativeBinomial, Geometric, MultivariateNormal and Multinomial responses.
  • Cox proportional hazards models: LP_to_Y(family = "Cox") simulates right-censored survival times (Weibull baseline hazard, exponential censoring), and Y_to_LP(family = "Cox") maps (time, status), or a survival::Surv() object, to the deviance residuals of the null Cox model for selection.
  • Generate_Beta() generates sparse coefficient vectors.

Documentation

  • A pkgdown website, https://yuchenxiao95.github.io/IChop/, with a function reference and one article, “An Introduction to IChop”, covering every response family and comparing the search with the lasso and adaptive lasso from glmnet.
  • citation("IChop") cites Xiao and Walker (2026).
